title: Unify ephemeral builders into hierarchical builder profiles with predictive cache priming
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our CI fleet has accumulated dozens of ad-hoc ephemeral builder images and per-language toolchain permutations. This increases image churn, cache miss rate, and flakiness during parallel builds. Objective: consolidate ephemeral builders into a small set of hierarchical builder profiles (base -> language overlay -> job-specific shim) and implement a predictive cache-priming service that pre-warms relevant CAS/artifacts ahead of CI runs to reduce cold-start latency and improve cache hit rate.
background_and_context: Over the last 18 months we've added language-specific builder images and temporary fast-fix images to unblock teams. Observability (pipeline timings, cache hit-rate) shows a median pipeline time regression of ~18% when cold caches occur; cross-repo flakes correlate with builder-image churn. Customer-impact (internal developer experience) is high: longer iteration, PRs blocked by flaky lint/builds. This ticket is part of the broader 'CI Modernization' initiative to reduce build latency and make builds more deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce hierarchical builder profiles and migrate 60% of CI jobs to profiles (base + overlay) without changing job-level commands
Increase CAS/artifact cache hit rate by >=20% for migrated jobs within two weeks of rollout
Reduce median CI pipeline time for full test builds by >=12% in migrated repos
Provide migration docs and a rollback plan; no net increase in maintenance surface for infra team
approach_and_solution_outline: Define 3-4 base builder images (minimal linux base, common tooling, docker/remote cache client)
Create small language overlays (nodejs, python, go, rust) built on top of base images as thin layers
Replace ad-hoc ephemeral images with job-specific lightweight shims (shell hooks) applied at runtime
Implement predictive priming: a service that watches PRs/branch activity and CI queue patterns, then pro-actively pulls and uploads likely-needed artifacts into CAS/registry before jobs start
Add CI-side heuristics to favor layered cache reuse (pinning layer digests, reuse manifests) and graceful fallbacks
Coordinate lint/toolchain upgrades via gated rollout jobs with compatibility checks and auto-rollback hooks
migration_plan_and_phases: Phase 0 (Now - 2w): Design and prototyping. Build minimal base + node overlay; smoke test with 10 low-risk repos
Phase 1 (2-6w): Expand overlays for python/go, instrument cache metrics and cache-priming service in passive mode (priming predictions logged but not executed)
Phase 2 (6-10w): Turn on active priming for selected pipelines, migrate 30% of non-critical jobs to profiles, monitor SLOs
Phase 3 (10-16w): Full migration of scheduled/owner-approved repos, enable toolchain upgrade gates for lint jobs
Phase 4 (16-20w): Harden and document, deprecate legacy ephemeral images, run a clean-up sweep
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with infra, devtools, and platform teams. Agreed on base image policy (stable LTS distro, stripped runtime, reproducible tags). Action: infra to publish initial base image recipe.

2026-02-18: Prototype base + node overlay completed. Smoke tests on three repos show 9-11% median pipeline time improvement when cache warm; cache miss path still expensive. Link to prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-builder-profiles/pull/42

2026-02-25: Implemented passive priming logger. Initial heuristic (recently-changed dependency graph + top-10 recently-run jobs) predicts artifacts with ~65% precision in lab. Logged metrics to: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci/cache-priming?orgId=1

2026-03-05: Engineering review: security team requested SBOMs for new images and KMS usage for registry credentials. Added security_review_required flag and checklist. Assigned to SecOps for approval.

2026-03-10: Ran a canary active priming experiment for 12 low-risk PRs. Observed 22% increase in CAS hit rate and 14% median pipeline time reduction. No security incidents. Preparing migration runbook and owner opt-in form.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Predictive priming could evict useful cache artifacts or overload storage network. Mitigation: Start with passive mode, cap parallel priming throughput, introduce backoff and cool-down windows based on storage metrics

Risk: Toolchain upgrades may surface lint/formatter regressions. Mitigation: Add gated compatibility job that runs upgraded toolchain only on a small set of changed files and collects diffs; auto-rollback if metric thresholds exceeded
Risk: Developers confused by new layered images. Mitigation: Provide clear docs, migration helper script to detect custom image usage and print recommended profile mapping
open_questions_and_decisions_needed: Q1: Do we embed language runtimes in overlays or rely on remote package caching (speed vs. image size trade-off)? Decision due 2026-03-16
Q2: Which ML/heuristic model to use for priming predictions (simple frequency + recency vs. lightweight classifier)? Action: prototype both and compare in passive mode
Q3: Retention policy for primed artifacts in CAS (TTL vs LRU). Proposal: TTL 30 days for primed artifacts, review after two months
qa_and_validation_plan: Define KPIs: CAS hit-rate, median pipeline time (full build), 95th percentile job latency, flaky-job-rate
Run A/B canary across 1000 pipelines over 2 weeks and collect violin plots for distribution shifts
Add e2e smoke test that runs in staging with forced cold-cache to validate fallback paths
rollout_and_rollback: Rollout: opt-in by repo owner for initial waves, then auto-suggest mapping for others; monitor for 72 hours before wider enablement
Rollback: revert job mapping to original ephemeral image and purge primed artifacts related to the repo; alert on rollback action and open incident review
owner_notes_and_next_steps: Owner (Liam): finalize decision on overlay vs remote runtime by 2026-03-16
Infra: provide signed base image and SBOM artifact by 2026-03-20
Devtools: open migration helper PR to detect custom images and emit mapping recommendations
